coaching.headline: Serath kept dying, every Fangtooth came our way, and it was over fast. Clean fucking work.
coaching.team: A quick, clean stomp in which Serath died seven times. We drew first blood, took all three Fangtooths, the Mini Prime and the only Seedling, and took two of their outer towers for one of ours. The sloppy patch came when Murdock and Khaimera both died shortly before our only lost tower, and Sparrow later won one exchange. Those were the only blemishes. The closing ace, followed by the last Fangtooth, finished it.

focus.title: Dead jungler, free pit
focus.evidence: Each of our three Fangtooths and the Mini Prime fell to us within a minute of a Serath death. The record does not show whether the pit was already up when Serath died or who started it.
focus.action: Next game, whenever the enemy jungler dies and a Fangtooth or Prime is up, Xeebs calls it and the two nearest players start it before the respawn. Check that every such death ends in a take.

perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim's Gadget was the cleanest game in the lobby: seven kills without a death, the richest player on the map, farm well above Willy's usual pace. Serath died to Gadget three times, a hell of a way to tell a jungler to stay home. The gold outran the damage, with hero damage under Willy's usual Gadget rate. When Riktor lands a pull or a suppress next game, Gadget drops Tesla Dome on that target.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs ran the map. First blood on Revenant, three kills on Serath, roughly two thirds of our objective damage and the most healing in the lobby: that is a jungler setting the tempo, not following it. The one lost exchange came when Sparrow killed Khaimera and Legion. Next game, when the enemy carry is alive in a fight, Khaimera saves Ambush for that carry once she is hurt, because the leap hits harder on a wounded target.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock topped our hero damage and kept punishing two enemy laners: Gideon died to Mr_Meat31 three times and Revenant twice. Fucking good. The recurring problem was Revenant himself, whose only two kills of the game were both on Murdock. If Revenant shows up next game with Reckoning available, Murdock keeps Buckshot for him: the push-back buys distance and the armor shred adds damage to the trade, so Revenant has to earn the next one.
perPlayer.3aa472b8-db6f-494b-967e-54c3408fc466: NO_LIFE_KING_HS kept Legion alive, one death against a usual count of nearly five, and opened the closing ace with kills on Zinx and Sparrow. Keep that restraint. The soft spot was output: hero damage ran more than a third under that player's own Legion norm. Press the Advantage drops a Rally Point at every takedown and speeds up Legion's fire, so when one lands mid-fight, Legion keeps shooting from inside it instead of backing off.
perPlayer.07237cc8-a80d-4b8b-ae3e-9347f8c34a9e: Riktor was a fucking wall: no deaths and the most damage mitigated in the lobby. The rest of the support job was thin. Riktor had a hand in under a third of our kills and placed three wards to Zinx's eight, clearing none. Rift Walkers raises the ward cap for exactly this. Before the next Fangtooth, Riktor spends every ward charge on the enemy approach and walks in with Riplash ready, so the pull starts the fight.

10.call: Gadget killed Gideon and then Serath, won 2-0, and our second Fangtooth fell shortly after. Kill credits do not show who was at the pit or who else was nearby.

13.7.call: Khaimera killed Revenant and Murdock killed Gideon, won 2-0, as their first Outer Tower fell in the same window, just after our Mini Prime. The timing does not show who hit the tower.

15.5.call: Sparrow killed Khaimera and Legion while Murdock took Revenant, lost 1-2, and we took their second Outer Tower in the same window. The record does not show whether those deaths bought the tower.

17.5.call: Won 5-0: Legion took Zinx and Sparrow, Khaimera took Serath and Gideon, Gadget took Revenant. Our third Fangtooth followed. Kill credits do not show where Murdock or Riktor were during it.

3aa472b8-db6f-494b-967e-54c3408fc466.matchup: Duo lane was Legion with Riktor into Sparrow with Zinx. Neither duo lost a player early, and first blood went our way through Khaimera. Sparrow later killed Khaimera and Legion in the one lost exchange, and Legion took Sparrow and Zinx in the closing ace. Zinx was the enemy healer, and Sparrow finished Vanquisher, which executes a hero who drops very low. Revenant and Serath added the rest of their physical damage.
3aa472b8-db6f-494b-967e-54c3408fc466.build: Manta Scythe adds physical penetration, attack speed and lifesteal, extra damage to minions and small monsters, and bonus damage against an enemy with no ally nearby. Resolution adds more physical penetration, on-hit damage and bonus power once its mana stacks fill. Both feed the K-75 Storm Rifle, whose damage rises with physical penetration owned. The common winning core is Malady, Deathstalker and Spear Of Desolation. Final inventory does not show purchase timing, and no fight here shows the build costing anything.
3aa472b8-db6f-494b-967e-54c3408fc466.eternal: Marrow heals Legion for a share of hero damage dealt, more at low health and less from area attacks. Blood Bank turns recent hero damage into extra lifesteal; Jealousy adds damage as Legion's health falls. That is a sustain-and-trade package for a rapid-fire carry, and one death says the survival side held, though the record cannot show Marrow's share of the healing. The Maw, bonus true damage on basic attacks into low-health targets, is the slot-two alternative when finishing matters more than trading from low health.
3aa472b8-db6f-494b-967e-54c3408fc466.augment: Press the Advantage spawns a Rally Point where a takedown happens. That Rally Point no longer heals, but it raises Legion's rate of fire and gives nearby allies attack speed. It pays in extended fights that produce takedowns, like the closing ace, and gives nothing in an exchange without a kill. The record does not show Rally Point uptime.
3aa472b8-db6f-494b-967e-54c3408fc466.crest: Eviscerator's active grants a short burst of attack speed, omnivamp and on-hit damage. It suits Legion's sustained fire and stacks with Marrow's healing during a committed fight. The record does not show when it was used.
3aa472b8-db6f-494b-967e-54c3408fc466.improvement: Survival held, so hero damage is the build question. Zinx healed and Serath built lifesteal, so Tainted Rounds is the comparison against Manta Scythe: healing reduction and on-hit damage on Legion's basic attacks, in exchange for Manta's penetration, lifesteal and faster farming. No enemy finished an armor item, so Deathstalker's armor shred is less urgent than anti-heal in this lobby. This win does not prove the swap was needed.

07237cc8-a80d-4b8b-ae3e-9347f8c34a9e.matchup: Support matchup was Riktor with Legion into Zinx with Sparrow. Zinx was their healer, and Riktor's pull, silence and suppress are the tools to start fights on her or Sparrow. Gideon's Astral Catalyst deals bonus damage to shielded targets, which matters because Riktor's Electrocute shield and Transference both lean on shields. Riktor did not die, and neither duo lost a player early.
07237cc8-a80d-4b8b-ae3e-9347f8c34a9e.build: Transference adds health, both armors and stronger heals and shields. While shielded, Riktor gains movement speed and extra armor, and an expiring shield returns part of its remaining value as health. Electrocute's shield is the natural trigger. It was the only finished item, and Riktor led the lobby in damage mitigated; the record does not show how much of that came from Transference.
07237cc8-a80d-4b8b-ae3e-9347f8c34a9e.eternal: Knell applies Rust on hero hits, shredding both armors and giving Riktor part of what it shreds. Patina grants a shield after a stretch without taking damage, and while it holds, Transference's movement speed and armor bonus are active. Resonant Repair heals and grants tenacity whenever Riktor is immobilized; the record does not show how often that happened. That favors a frontline support who trades hits, and Riktor's zero deaths say the durability side held.
07237cc8-a80d-4b8b-ae3e-9347f8c34a9e.augment: Zap O' 9-Chains makes Riktor's next basic attack after an ability cast zap nearby enemies. It turns ability casts into extra damage in grouped fights. It adds no crowd control, so the pull, silence and suppress remain the main job. The record does not show how often the zap fired.
07237cc8-a80d-4b8b-ae3e-9347f8c34a9e.crest: Rift Walkers gives a dash that pulls nearby heroes, a second engage tool beside Riplash and Skewer. Its Visionary passive grants Solstone and raises the ward cap, so the crest was built for vision work; three wards placed against Zinx's eight does not reflect that extra capacity. Reduced gold from minion kills is the support trade-off it carries.
07237cc8-a80d-4b8b-ae3e-9347f8c34a9e.improvement: The winning core is Dynamo, Xenia and Frosted Lure. Dynamo makes immobilized enemies take more damage briefly, a direct fit with Riplash and Skewer, and Xenia shields allies within close range. Compared with Transference, that trades Riktor's own shield value for damage and protection the team shares. Riktor never died and had a hand in under a third of our kills, so survival already held and the next item should serve participation.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.matchup: Offlane opponent was Revenant, who finished Terminus and Vanquisher and got both of his kills on Murdock. Murdock killed Revenant twice and Gideon three times. Revenant's Reckoning pulls a single target into a separate realm with him and slows them, forcing a one-on-one. Serath and Sparrow added the rest of their physical threat.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Lightning Hawk builds charge while moving or attacking and empowers a basic attack with bonus damage and a slow. Vanquisher adds physical power, penetration and critical chance, and executes a hero who drops very low. Both add critical chance; neither adds sustain or defense. They are the first two items of the common winning core, and no fight here shows the build costing anything.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Vermis rewards three consecutive basic attacks on the same hero with max-health damage, and Serration adds missing-health damage to that hit. Melting Point only adds damage against targets above a high physical armor threshold, and no enemy finished an armor item, so it had little to trigger on; the record cannot show whether any target crossed it. Sub-Surface, less damage from area abilities, is the slot-two alternative against Gideon's area spells.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.augment: Justice's Reach makes Shots Fired, the empowered shot after five basic attacks, pierce units and reach farther. It rewards poking from a safe distance and firing through the wave. The record does not show how many empowered shots landed.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.crest: Pacifier dashes, empowers the next physical hit, deals much more damage to low-health targets and allows a recast after a kill. It is both the finisher and the exit. Against Revenant's Reckoning, the dash is the tool to hold back; the record does not show when it was used.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.improvement: Imperator completes the winning core and raises critical strike damage on top of the critical chance already owned, the natural next item. If Revenant keeps finding Murdock first, a defensive slot is the alternative, trading that crit damage for survival in the duel. This match does not prove either choice was needed.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.matchup: Mid opponent was Gideon, the enemy's main magical damage dealer, who finished Astral Catalyst and Overseer. Gadget killed Gideon twice and Serath three times without dying. Serath's dive is the kit-level threat to an immobile mage, and Security Gate's root is the answer Gadget's kit provides.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Soulbinder adds power, mana and ability haste, deals bonus damage on ability hits from long range, and slowly adds permanent power when that triggers. Azure Core stacks mana from kills for bonus power and gives a low-health shield. Oblivion Crown raises total magical power by a large percentage. The winning core runs Entropy and Overseer instead of Soulbinder and Oblivion Crown. The record does not show Soulbinder's long-range triggers, and no fight shows the build costing anything.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Aion converts spell damage to heroes into gold and stacks mana regeneration on casts. Bottomless Vial rewards River Buffs Gadget personally kills with a potion charge and permanent power; river buffs split evenly, and the record does not show whose they were. Runic Focus scales power with current mana, which suits Azure Core and Soulbinder's mana pools. Perfection, ability haste while health stays above a high threshold, is the slot-two alternative for a mage who did not die.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.augment: Auto-Lock Amp makes the Seek and Destroy droid home faster onto the hero beneath it, making its damage zone harder to walk out of. Its value depends on stopping the droid over a hero, which the record cannot show.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.crest: Tempest damages up to three nearby heroes over several seconds and heals for part of that damage. It is a close-range tool on an immobile mage, so it pays when Gadget is already in the middle of the fight, such as inside Tesla Dome. The record does not show its use.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.improvement: The gold outran the damage. Overseer, from the winning core, makes Tesla Dome hit harder and heals Gadget for part of the ultimate's damage to heroes, a direct boost to the main teamfight tool. Entropy adds extra damage to each ability hit. Compared with Soulbinder, both give up the long-range bonus for steadier damage in close fights. This win does not prove the swap; it is the next comparison.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Jungle opponent was Serath, who died seven times, three of them to Khaimera, and got both of her kills on Khaimera. Khaimera's other kills came on Revenant twice and Gideon once. The enemy ran three physical damage dealers, Sparrow, Revenant and Serath, plus Zinx's healing, and Sparrow took the third Khaimera death in the one lost exchange.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Ashbringer adds attack speed, critical chance and ability haste and cuts current non-ultimate cooldowns on each basic attack, more on critical hits. Claw Of Hermes adds magical power, health, regeneration and mana, drains enemy mana on hit for true damage and raises ability damage against targets missing mana. Its magical power also gives Unleash extra attacks. Neither item adds armor. Khaimera took the most damage in the lobby; the record does not show which enemy dealt it.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Exarch is a support Eternal here: healing or shielding a target, Khaimera included, grants attack speed and magical on-hit damage for a few seconds, and Invigorate's heal is a clear trigger. Revelation shortens basic cooldowns on each cast; Fervour heals Khaimera and nearby allies on basic attacks against heroes. Marrow is the bruiser alternative, trading the team healing for lifesteal that grows at low health. The record cannot show Exarch uptime.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Jungle Invasion adds physical power in the jungle, scaling with level and doubled in the enemy jungle. It rewards invading, and Serath's deaths fit that plan, though the record does not show where those kills happened.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Judgement's active deals area damage around Khaimera and heals on hero hits on a short cooldown, plus omnivamp. It fits a sustain duelist and adds to healing that led the lobby; the record does not show its share.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: The armor gap is the build question. Khaimera finished with no armor against three physical threats while absorbing the most damage in the lobby. Sky Splitter and Onixian Quiver complete the winning core: current-health damage with lifesteal, then attack speed, crit and mitigation that grows with missing health. If Serath or Sparrow keep finding the kill next game, compare an armor item against Claw Of Hermes, trading Unleash's extra attacks and the mana burn for survival.

threats: Heal-stacking: Zinx. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s), Gadget Security Gate (root 1s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Riplash pull → Shock Therapy silence → Skewer suppress ult
ourKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
ourKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
ourKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

ourKits.combo: Security Gate root → Sticky Mine → Tesla Dome zone ult
ourKits.winCondition: root with the gate and trap a fight inside the Tesla Dome
ourKits.passive: FDA stacks grant scaling magical power
ourKits.playWith: frontline that holds enemies in her Dome
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge the gate; spread vs the Dome — she's immobile, dive her

ourKits.combo: Ambush leap → Unleash AS → Cull stun, Invigorate to cleanse+heal
ourKits.winCondition: stick on one target, stun with Cull and out-sustain via Spirit Regen
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his Cull stun
ourKits.playAgainst: ANTI-HEAL is mandatory — it guts his whole kit; kite the leap and CC through Invigorate

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
enemyKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
enemyKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

enemyKits.combo: Scar mark → Obliterate homing missiles → Reckoning 1v1 realm ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Reckoning a target into the Nether Realm and crit them down 1v1
enemyKits.playWith: a team to clean up if his 1v1 stalls
enemyKits.playAgainst: the ult is a 1v1 — peel the realmed ally can't help, so don't be caught alone; he's crit-reliant early-weak

enemyKits.combo: Ricochet stun → Bad Medicine zone → Infuse heal an ally → Neural Regenesis revive
enemyKits.winCondition: keep an ally alive with Infuse + the revive ult and poke with Ricochet
enemyKits.playWith: a carry she can pocket-heal and revive
enemyKits.playAgainst: she can't heal herself — dive HER; bait the revive before committing

enemyKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
enemyKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
enemyKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
enemyKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up
